recipes.name: Quick Sardine Curry
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon Thai red curry paste, or more to taste
1 (3.75 ounce) can sardines in oil, drained

steps.text: Heat canola oil in a skillet. Stir in red curry paste; cook and stir 3 to 5 seconds. Add shallot and garlic; cook and stir until fragrant. Add sardines; cook and stir until skins slightly browned and coated in paste mixture. Gently stir in coconut cream; toss to coat sardines. Bring mixture to a boil and cook until sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Sardine Curry
raw_recipe.description: This quick sardine curry stir-fry recipe is made with canned sardines and a simple coconut curry sauce with Thai flavors. It is delicious with rice.

review.reviewBody: Good way to eat sardines. I varied it based on ingredients at hand. I used green Thai curry paste, substituted rice milk for coconut cream (No coconut cream/milk on hand, and thought regular milk would curdle), stirfried a stalk of celery first, and added some minced candied ginger.

Easy to make, quick, delicious and filling. Makes for a quick dinner when you don't want anything too complicated. Add vegetables on the step when you add the shallot and garlic (made it with celery and bell peppers). Didn't make it with coconut cream and still tasted fine.

I've been eating sardines for 50 years but never thought to do this. Great recipe. I used cashew milk instead of coconut cream and I added a can of stewed tomatoes, and a little sugar to balance the acidity. It will now be on my regular rotation for a quick dinner.

My wife was stunned. She anticipated spitting it out; instead, I couldn't get my plate back and had to prep a second can.

Changes: used green curry paste, 2 cloves garlic, 2 scallions in place of shallot, and cashew cream in place of coconut.

This was absolutely amazing! I did modify it with what I had in my cabinet, but still, outstanding! I used butter instead of canola oil, yellow onion instead of shallot, and heavy whipping cream instead of coconut cream. Flipping delicious! I would eat this for every meal. And I made this with the cheap store brand sardines, not even fancy ones.

I really liked this recipe. I added chopped cilantro to the mix to give it even more flavor, and spinach too. I also added green onions instead of scallions, and it gave it a more well-rounded flavor.

What a delightful recipe with room for customization! I used massamun curry paste and added chopped tomatoes and frozen peas to use up some veggies. Coconut cream is good, just adds more calories. 

Served over black rice for some added iron. Will make again and again.

Fabulous meal in just a few minutes. Used wild caught sardines, coconut oil instead of canola oil and coconut milk instead of coconut cream. Served it on mashed potatoes that I moistened with a little coconut milk. Delish!
I accidently added 'cream of coconut' but it was still yummy - more spicey-hot with a sweet edge... I added a can of petite diced tomatoes at the end, mmmmmm. Next time I will serve it over rice!!

Yummy! (And I generally don't like sardines!) I accidentally bought cream of coconut, which added a sweetness that paired well with the heat. I mixed in cooked rice at the end. I will be making this again!
I adjusted the recipe based on 2 sardines. Awesome!!! Loved it and will make again as it’s easy, fast and healthy.

Holy moly this is good. I made it almost a year ago and I still remember my surprise when it turned out amazing the first time. I went heavy on the curry paste and cooked my rice in chicken broth. It was absolutely amazing. You don't even taste the sardines.
this will be a go-to recipe!
Not as spicy as I thought it would be, which is good. It dresses up the sardines nicely. I smashed up the fish as it cooked. I’m looking forward to eating the rest for lunch tomorrow.
delicious and Easy. don't skip coconut cream, adds some complexity to the flavor
My family just isn't fond of sardines! I don't think I'll make this again.

I made a quintuple batch with a 1 lb can of sardines in tomato sauce. Added a pound of sauteed cubed tofu. Served it over rice. The husband "tolerated" it, he said, but ate every bit; both teenaged sons liked it (!) and ate it up; the housemate and I liked it a lot. There are no leftovers.

Loved this. Only deviated once with coconut milk - not cream. I enjoyed this with my homemade crackers made from the pulp of my morning green juicing ritual. Already looking forward to making this again. So easy and yummy. Thanks for posting

Made exactly except that I used the green end of scallions instead of shallots. Came out great, but was even better after a day in the fridge and used as a fish dip for crackers. Will definitely be taking it to the next party.
I didn't have coconut cream, so I just left it out. It tastes just fine without it and makes a nice savory appetizer.
